_readme: What each character level costs in experience, one row per level, from 2 up to RewardTrack.MaxLevel. There is no formula: this replaced a geometric curve (c=100, g=1.09, cap 200) in progression v2 phase 2, because a formula that fit the early levels priced the late ones at four to five deep runs and vice versa - see docs/handoffs/progression_v2/PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md section 3 for the shape and xp_model.md Part C for the three fits that failed. `cost` is the cost to ENTER that level, so `level: 2` is what a fresh level-1 character pays for their first level-up, and the cumulative cost to reach level 40 is the sum of every row. Three rules the resolver enforces and an author has to hold in mind while editing: the table must cover levels 2..MaxLevel with no gaps and no duplicates; costs must never DECREASE as level rises (a cheaper level later reads as a bug in every screen that says 'about N fights to go'); and every cost must sit between 58 and 10153 inclusive, which is the plan's contract 2 - 58 is two typical room-0 fights, the floor below which a level is not an event, and 10153 is one full deep run's pay at 25 permille, the ceiling above which a level costs more than the longest run in the game. Changing the cap means changing RewardTrack.MaxLevel and this table together; the resolver refuses a table that does not match it. Field-by-field documentation and defaults: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.
